hypotheses.justification: hV is only used to build hF, the argument of supCode_le_iff, which gives supCode c {V,W} ⊆ U. That inclusion holds without hV. Take p ∈ supCode c {V,W} = regular c (⋃{V,W}). By mem_regular, p ∈ c and for every q ∈ c with p ⊆ q there is r ∈ ⋃{V,W} with q ⊆ r. Since V ⊆ U and W ⊆ U (h.1, h.2.1), r ∈ U. So the same condition holds for U, and mem_regular gives p ∈ regular c U. Then regular c U = U by hU.2, so p ∈ U. The reverse inclusion in the proof uses only hU, h and mem_regular, not hV. So hV can be deleted. Deleting hW works the same way, and both can be deleted together.

hW is only used to build hF for supCode_le_iff, which gives supCode c {V,W} ⊆ U. Replace that step by the direct monotonicity argument. For p ∈ regular c (⋃{V,W}), mem_regular gives p ∈ c and, for each q ∈ c with p ⊆ q, some r ∈ ⋃{V,W} with q ⊆ r. Here r ∈ V or r ∈ W, and both are ⊆ U by h, so r ∈ U. Hence p ∈ regular c U = U, using hU.2. The other inclusion never uses hW. The statement stays true and provable without hW, and without hV.
